name: Monika Santra
title: PhD Candidate · Penn State
tagline: PhD candidate at Penn State working on software & systems security — binary analysis, control-flow recovery, vulnerability discovery, and malware analysis, augmented with AI/ML for practical reverse engineering at scale.
about: I am a PhD candidate in the Security of Software (SOS) Group at Penn State, advised by Dr. G. Gary Tan. My research sits at the intersection of program analysis and machine learning, focusing on making static analysis of compiled binaries practical, scalable, and precise — and more recently on agentic security: characterizing capability boundaries and attack surfaces of LLM-based autonomous agents.

Before Penn State, I spent five years as a Research Scientist at Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), India's premier nuclear research facility, where I built trusted systems, industrial control-network security tooling, and ensemble malware classifiers for host protection.

I hold an M.Tech from IIT Roorkee (CGPA 9.765/10, DGFS Fellow, DAE) and a B.Tech from Govt. College of Engineering & Textile Technology, Serampore. I ranked in the top 0.1% nationally in GATE CS 2015.
contact_note: I am open to research collaborations, invited talks, and PhD industry internship opportunities in program analysis, systems security, and AI/ML for software security.
